senses.definition: (heading) Physical appendage.
examples: He has a tag hung on his bag.

subsenses.definition: A skin tag, an excrescence of skin.
A dangling lock of sheep's wool, matted with dung; a dung tag.
Any slight appendage, as to an article of dress; something slight hanging loosely.
A metallic binding, tube, or point, at the end of a string, or lace, to stiffen it.
(biochemistry) Any short peptide sequence artificially attached to proteins mostly in order to help purify, solubilize or visualize these proteins.
Something mean and paltry; the rabble, originally refer to rag as torn cloth.

quotes.text: For upon the like Proclamation there, they all came in, both tag and rag

senses.definition: (heading) Last nonphysical appendage.

subsenses.definition: The last line (or last two lines) of a song's chorus that is repeated to indicate the end of the song.
(television) The last scene of a TV program, often focusing on the program's subplot.

quotes.text: Often, the tag punctuates the "we're all in this together" theme and is topped with a laugh.

subsenses.definition: The end, or catchword, of an actor's speech; cue.

senses.definition: (heading) Nonphysical label.

subsenses.definition: (informal, authorship) An attribution in narrated dialogue (eg, "he said") or attributed words (e.g. "he thought").

subsenses.definition: (computing) A piece of markup representing an element in a markup language.
examples: The <title> tag provides a title for the Web page.
The <sarcasm> tag conveys sarcasm in Internet slang.

subsenses.definition: (computing) A keyword, term, or phrase associated with or assigned to data, media, and/or information enabling keyword-based classification; often used to categorize content.
examples: I want to add genre and artist tags to the files in my music collection.

senses.definition: (heading) Identity.

subsenses.definition: (chiefly US) A vehicle number plate; a medal bearing identification data (animals, soldiers).
examples: The subwoofer in the trunk was so loud, it vibrated the tag like an aluminum can.

senses.definition: (heading) Involving being tagged physically.

subsenses.definition: (uncountable) A game, especially for children on playgrounds, in which one player (known as "it") attempts to touch another, who then becomes "it"; any similar game of chasing and trying to reach, touch, shoot, or label other players.
(baseball) An instance of touching the baserunner with the ball or the ball in a gloved hand to rule him "out."
examples: The tag was applied at second for the final out.

senses.definition: (heading) Signature.

subsenses.definition: (graffiti slang) Graffiti in the form of a stylized signature particular to the artist.

quotes.text: There is a hierarchy of sorts: a throw-up can go over a tag, a piece over a throw-up, and a burner over a piece.

senses.definition: A type of cardboard.
A sheep in its first year.

quotes.text: After being weaned, the ram or wedder lamb is sometimes termed hog, hoggit, or tag, during the whole of the first year
quotes.reference: 1807, The Complete Farmer, or, General Dictionary of Agriculture and Husbandry, →OCLC:

senses.definition: (transitive) To label (something).
(transitive) To mark (something) with one's graffiti tag.
(transitive) To remove dung tags from a sheep.
examples: Regularly tag the rear ends of your sheep.

senses.definition: (transitive, baseball, colloquial) To hit the ball hard.
(transitive, vulgar, slang, 1990s) to have sex with someone (especially a man of a woman)
examples: Steve is dying to tag Angie from chemistry class.

senses.definition: (transitive, baseball) To put a runner out by touching them with the ball or the ball in a gloved hand.
examples: He tagged the runner for the out.

senses.definition: (transitive, computing) To mark with a tag (metadata for classification).
examples: I am tagging my music files by artist and genre.

senses.definition: (transitive, Internet) To attach the name of (a user) to a posted message so that they are linked from the post and possibly sent a notification.

quotes.text: One side wants to demonstrate a higher level of street knowledge and openly denounces the distorting lens of Instagram dissings; the other embraces the medium's branding affordances by sending “clout” to a third-party ally, while at the same time avoiding tagging the opponent.

senses.definition: To follow closely, accompany, tag along.

quotes.text: A tall young man came striding through the park along the path near which she sat. Behind him tagged a boy carrying a suit-case.

senses.definition: (transitive) To catch and touch (a player in the game of tag).
(transitive) To fit with, or as if with, a tag or tags.

quotes.text: He learned to make long-tagged thread laces.

senses.definition: (transitive, online gaming, slang) To make contact with an enemy, usually by attacking it before other players do, to establish exclusive or partial eligibility for loot, experience points achievements, etc.
examples: He keeps tagging my mobs and I miss out on all the drops.
I can fight her for you, but you have to tag her if you want the achievement.
